rv.q: In its strongest moments, the “play with music” adaptation of Susanna Kaysen’s memoir Girl, Interrupted captures the riptide sensation of being pulled far from safe shores and unsure of how you got there or how to get back.
But trying to approximate Kaysen’s reportorial chill makes her onstage avatar theatrically inert.
The musical never acquires dramatic momentum.
Like its predecessors in print and onscreen, ultimately this latest rendition of Girl, Interrupted raises more questions than it answers.
Girl, Interrupted is a sturdy showcase for Mann’s gorgeous, shimmering-sad compositions, but perhaps a less successful conduit for Kaysen’s arguments.
This production sweeps you into its arms before you have a chance to refuse, and when it releases you the world around you has changed.
Fans of Mann and Marjok, as well as theatergoers truly interested in viewing fresh, vital, new works of music drama should try to get a ticket to this compelling production.
The secret weapon of Girl, Interrupted, the play, is Aimee Mann.

Majok emphasizes the bond developed between the protagonist and the other inmates. Their shared experiences of trauma and misogyny and feelings of oppression provide a strong connection. One of the most moving scenes involves Susannah and her friends visiting a patient in the violent ward.

The show is more compelling when it begins to look at other characters besides Susanna, and how they deal with the pressures of the outside world—or don’t. Still, Majok tries to thread the needle between recapturing the interiority and fragmentary storytelling of the memoir and the Hollywoodized drama of the film with uneven results.

Majok’s adaptation confronts the systemic failures of the system in which these women are trapped with clear-eyed forthrightness, while Bonney ensures their depths of despair are always simmering under the surface—and, very occasionally, boil up without warning.
The musical adaptation of Girl, Interrupted takes care to adapt Susanna Kaysen’s memoir with thoughtfulness and respect, coupled with original music by Aimee Mann.
There's plenty of beautiful, delicate, heartfelt work in the mix. But whatever the blend of complicating pathologies, this girl still feels fettered.
Regrettably, though, while Mann’s lyrics aim for anguished poetry, they occasionally only induce winces.
While the show was an almost a decade in the making – interrupted by the COVID pandemic -- "Girl, Interrupted" still really needs more time in development to be completely effective.
The spectacular new musical, Girl, Interrupted now at the Public Theater in Manhattan.
Girl, Interrupted celebrates the strength in sisterhood, the power of music and storytelling to find meaning in the darkest episodes of human experience.
Aimee Mann’s breathtaking music gives this melancholy adaptation a beating heart
Girl, Interrupted is doing something genuinely difficult: rendering the texture of a disordered memory with theatrical and musical honesty, without sentimentality and without exploitation.
Atmospherically rich and thematically urgent, Girl, Interrupted is held back by a script that observes more than it inhabits.

cn.t: Critics find this musical adaptation of Kaysen's memoir achingly beautiful but uneven, praising Canfield's performance and Mann's haunting score while noting issues with pacing and structure.
